title: Bandung Conference (Asian–African Conference)
summary: From 18 to 24 April 1955 twenty-nine Asian and African governments met at Bandung, Indonesia, with Burma, India, Indonesia, Pakistan and Sri Lanka as sponsors. The closing communiqué called for economic and cultural cooperation, self-determination, human rights and an end to racial discrimination, and the conference laid the foundation for the nonaligned movement.

uncertainty.note: Exact days from the Google Arts & Culture page; the State Department page says only April 1955.

where.modern_name: Gedung Merdeka, Bandung, West Java, Indonesia

importance.justification: First large conference of Asian and African states, a foundation for the nonaligned movement.
